text:
liam_fin: FYI got an email from a Colombia supplier (NubeLabs SAS). They attached an invoice and are asking Redwood to "gross-up" for retefuente withholding.

liam_fin: invoice snippet they pasted:
`````
Invoice #NL-2025-042
Supplier: NubeLabs SAS (NIT 900.123.456-7)
Service: Platform integration + monthly support
Amount (COP): 10,000,000
Requested retefuente: 7.0% (700,000)
Supplier asks Redwood to gross-up so they receive full 10,000,000
`````

liam_fin: They also attached a PDF titled "Certificado de Residencia" issued by DIAN (in Spanish). Question: do we gross-up or withhold? Need tax confirmation before tomorrow's payment run.

marcela_tax: thanks. Initial thoughts: retefuente rates depend on payment type. For domestic suppliers with a Colombian NIT, standard practice is to withhold unless there's a DIAN exemption. The certificate you mention usually proves residency, not exemption. Can you upload the PDF here?

liam_fin: uploaded PDF to this thread (stamp from DIAN, valid through 2025).

kevin_payments: holding payment until tax confirms. If we gross-up we need an explicit PO/contract clause that Redwood pays withholding. Do we have that?

oliver_legal: checked SOW/MSA. No gross-up clause. Vendor responsibility for taxes is the default. Commercial team can negotiate but finance shouldn't do unilateral gross-ups.

marcela_tax: two options: if vendor is Colombian tax resident (NIT present) we withhold retefuente (7%) and remit to DIAN. If vendor claims non-resident treaty exemption they must provide DIAN-issued exemption or foreign tax residency docs plus tax approval. The attached certificate looks like a Colombian residency cert -> implies domestic, so withholding applies.

liam_fin: vendor's email says "we sent certificate to avoid withholding, please gross-up so we can receive full amount." They also sent bank confirmation.

oliver_legal: vendor request to gross-up without contract support is commercial. We can escalate to Commercial, but no unilateral payment changes.

kevin_payments: practical math: withhold 7% => vendor gets COP 9,300,000, remit COP 700,000 to DIAN. If Product wants vendor made whole, open a PO change for gross-up amount and legal approval.

jess_ops: passing to Product. Is vendor receiving net payment urgent for go-live?

sana_product: Pilot timeline is tight but not critical. Ask vendor to accept net payment for now; we can evaluate a commercial credit if needed.

marcela_tax: recommended next steps:
1) Ask vendor to confirm in writing they are Colombian tax resident (they essentially already did).
2) Proceed to withhold per DIAN rules and remit.
3) If vendor insists on gross-up, request an official DIAN exemption specific to this withholding or written tax legal opinion from their advisor; tax will review.

liam_fin: I'll reply: we will withhold per Colombian tax rules; if you provide DIAN exemption we'll review. Copying legal.

oliver_legal: please cc contracts@redwood and ask vendor to acknowledge net payment acceptance in writing.

kevin_payments: payment flagged on HOLD until tax confirms or we receive commercial approval.

liam_fin: sending reply now. :thumbsup:

payments-bot: Payment #PR-5412 placed on HOLD for supplier NubeLabs SAS - reason: tax documentation review. Will notify when released.

marcela_tax: tagging for follow-up next week; if DIAN exemption arrives we can reconsider but default is to withhold.

liam_fin: noted. Closing thread when vendor replies.
